what_its_for: Fremanezumab-vfrm is used to prevent migraine headaches in adults. It does not treat a migraine that has already started. It works by blocking a protein in the body called CGRP, which plays a role in causing migraines. Using this medicine regularly can help reduce how often you get migraines and how severe they are.
how_to_take: This medicine comes as a liquid in a prefilled autoinjector pen or prefilled syringe and is given as a shot under the skin (subcutaneous injection). You will inject it into your stomach area (abdomen), upper thigh, or the back of your upper arm. Do not inject into skin that is tender, bruised, red, or hard. Before injecting, let the pen or syringe sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes — do not warm it in a microwave or hot water. Clean the injection site with an alcohol wipe and let it dry before injecting. Your doctor, nurse, or pharmacist will show you how to give yourself the injection. Always use a new pen or syringe for each dose and never reuse or share your device with anyone else. Dispose of used pens and syringes in an approved sharps container right away.
dosing: There are two dosing options your doctor will choose for you. Option 1 — Monthly dosing: You inject 225 mg (one prefilled pen or syringe) under the skin once every month. Option 2 — Quarterly dosing: You inject 675 mg (three prefilled pens or syringes given one after another at the same visit) under the skin once every three months. If you give three injections in one sitting, choose three different spots on your body or at least 2 inches apart on the same area. Follow your doctor's instructions exactly about which schedule is right for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, inject your missed dose as soon as you remember. Then restart your dosing schedule from the date you gave the missed injection. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist for guidance. Do not give two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store your prefilled pens or syringes in the refrigerator at 36°F to 46°F (2°C to 8°C). Keep them in the original carton to protect them from light. Do not freeze fremanezumab-vfrm, and do not use it if it has been frozen. If needed, you may store it at room temperature (up to 77°F or 25°C) for up to 3 months. Once you take it out of the refrigerator and store it at room temperature, do not put it back in the refrigerator. Write the date you removed it from the refrigerator on the carton. Throw it away if it has been at room temperature for more than 3 months or if the expiration date has passed. Keep out of reach of children.
what_to_avoid: There are no specific foods, drinks, or activities you must strictly avoid while using this medicine. However, always tell your doctor about all other medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take, as drug interactions are possible. Avoid injecting into skin that is irritated, scarred, tattooed, or affected by a skin condition. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery if you feel unwell after your injection until you know how this medicine affects you.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency medical help right away if you have any signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as: rash or hives anywhere on your body, swelling of your face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing or swallowing, dizziness, or feeling faint. These can happen within hours to one month after your injection. Also contact your doctor if the injection site becomes very red, swollen, or painful, if your migraines are not improving after a few months of treatment, if you become pregnant or plan to become pregnant, or if you have any new or unusual symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: You may start to notice fewer migraines within the first month of treatment, but it can take up to 3 months to feel the full benefit. Keep using your injections as scheduled even if you do not notice improvement right away. Do not stop using this medicine without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. The effects of this medicine on an unborn baby or nursing infant are not fully known. Your doctor will help you weigh the benefits and risks. Kidney or liver problems: No dose adjustment is generally needed, but let your doctor know about any kidney or liver conditions you have. Older adults (65 and older): This medicine has been used in older adults, but tell your doctor about all your health conditions and medicines so they can make sure it is safe for you. Children: This medicine is not approved for use in people under 18 years of age.
